newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen firm on JGB rise, BOJ accomodative.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen firm on JGB rise, BOJ accomodative.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures firmed on the back of gains in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures on Thursday but dealers said trading was relatively featureless and thin with many players out for the Labour Day holiday.
Euroyen futures remained in positive territory for much of the session despite steep gains in Tokyo stocks in early trade.
Dealers said the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s generous money market operation boosted Euroyen futures as it was above market expectations.
"The BOJ injected twice what was expected so the overnight rate couldn't stay too high," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.
The Japanese central bank injected a net 200 billion yen into the money market on Thursday, against a projected fund surplus of 90 billion yen.

A trader with a U.S. institution said Euroyen and JGB futures also benefited from data showing a 12.7 percent drop in Japan's April domestic vehicle sales, marking the first year-on-year decline in eight months.
"Euroyen have been quite firm all day. There was good paper buying all the way up," he said, adding that December Euroyen would face resistance around 99.05.
The contract was quoted at 99.02 at 1100 GMT against its IMM close at 98.99 on light volume of 8,261 lots. June JGBs closed at 125.38 against their previous close at 125.09.
Eurodollar futures were scarcely changed with the December contract at 93.635 against its IMM close at 93.630 on volume of 5,405 lots.
